description: P2-08 G3 response-corpus axes, applicability exclusions (each with its reason) and the deterministic constrained pairwise covering executed by tests/systemic/test_response_corpus.py. Generated by tools/pairwise.py.

exclusions.reason: JSON-root kinds (array/string/null/number/truncated) are only observable where the response contract is a JSON chart payload: the daily and hourly ChartData reads and the history chunk read. The dashboard, chart-setup POST and the login/ACS handshakes never parse a JSON chart root.

CAPTCHA/security-step challenges are raised by the authentication gateway, not by a data endpoint, and the dashboard gateway does not classify the challenge page as terminal (pseg_client.py:1804-1855 only checks the login bounce and the verification token). The corpus excludes both from the daily chart stage for the same reason; the login POST keeps them.

A 307/308 only exercises the credential-preserving re-POST on the chart-setup POST. Every other stage is a GET read, and the login POST and the SAML ACS are sent with allow_redirects=False and refused/verified as a redirect (pseg_client.py:1237-1300) rather than re-POSTed.

The login POST classifier distinguishes only HTTP >= 500, the CAPTCHA phrase/flag and the JSON error fields (pseg_client.py:1139-1169); any other 200/4xx/3xx body returns empty Data and is then confirmed through /Dashboard, so its declared invalidity is indistinguishable from a successful sign-in at that handshake. 500/503, timeout, connection error, CAPTCHA and valid_success stay.

The real login form read is GET / (pseg_client._login_form_token, :1097-1108): it checks only status >= 500 and extracts the antiforgery token, and it classifies neither redirects nor challenges. Any 200/4xx/3xx body without that token, including a CAPTCHA page, simply supplies an empty token and the flow proceeds to the login POST, so the declared invalidity is unobservable there. 500/503, timeout, connection error and the valid form stay.
A 302 from the SAML ACS is the successful handoff back to the portal, not a signed-out login bounce; the corpus 302_login reply describes the dashboard/chart gateway.

keepalive() validates only the /Dashboard path and status (pseg_client.py:1658-1697): without the poll's antiforgery-token check a 200 HTML body is indistinguishable from a healthy dashboard, so a declared-invalid content body is unobservable there and its quarantine claim unenforceable. The setup/poll token path keeps these kinds.

A 302 login bounce is completed by requests itself: a Set-Cookie on the bounce is applied before the client can roll the jar back, so the redirect hop necessarily carries it. That hop is the transport finishing the same issued request, not a new client dispatch (the P2-01/P2-06 in-flight rule). The jar rollback contract stays covered by the 401/403 and 5xx cases, which do not redirect; the redirect shape is covered cookie-free.
Dashboard verification and the daily chart are mandatory for statistics authority and can never be optional legs (corpus.EXCLUSION_RULES).
History chunks are mandatory per-chunk reads and an auth handshake is never an optional enrichment; the optional position is the hourly leg only.

The pre-proof position is the auth-gateway segment before proof; chart and history reads happen only after the verified Dashboard token, so a pre-proof data read describes sequencing production cannot reach.
The optional enrichment leg is the hourly chart read of setup/poll; keepalive and backfill have no optional leg.
No flow's keepalive() requests chart or history routes: L/R/H keepalive is the single Dashboard GET, and S keepalive is SignIn -> ACS -> Dashboard (P2-06 FLOW_PLANS, tests/support/boundaries.py:204).

An expired keepalive session is handled as a typed auth failure or the Okta round trip (pseg_client.py:1080-1091, :1389-1400): _renew refuses to post the saved password while _in_keepalive, and no flow loads the local login form during keepalive.

Only the legacy SSO flow's keepalive performs the Okta SignIn -> ACS -> Dashboard round trip (P2-06 FLOW_PLANS S keepalive, tests/support/boundaries.py:204), which P2-05's reviewed policy permits as the current-owner SAML relay. Local, Remember-Me and human keepalive is a Dashboard-only GET, so an ACS reply there is unreachable.
backfill walks the Dashboard token plus one chart-setup/ChartData pair per history chunk; it has no daily/hourly poll leg and no login/ACS handshake.
Entry setup runs the Dashboard token plus daily/hourly legs. History is a service call, and the login form/POST and ACS handshakes need an expired session that a fresh declared jar does not present.
The MyMeter email/password login handshake (form GET and credential POST) is the local renewal only: R renews with RememberMe, S with Okta SAML and H carries human-pasted cookies.
The Okta SAML ACS autopost exists only in the legacy SSO flow S.
SSO mode relies solely on Okta idx/sid cookies; the portal RememberMe cookie is not used (corpus.EXCLUSION_RULES).
A CAPTCHA/security-step challenge is pre-authentication and never issues a session cookie; the corpus declares both kinds cookie-ineligible.

The chart-setup POST and the SAML ACS handshake are judged by status and handoff only: their bodies are never parsed, so a content kind there would be unobservable and its declared invalidity unenforceable.

The dashboard token GET is the one client entry point that re-raises a declared-transient requests exception unchanged (pseg_client.py:1796-1800); the P2-04 I10 observation treats a coordinator UpdateFailed as typed only when its cause is a PsegError. The client-family cases prove the typed-transport contract for these kinds; the HA family would assert that oracle fixture gap instead of an auth invariant.

Corpus fixture gap (reported for P2-03/P2-09): the P2-03 security-step builder is an HTML page, while production classifies the terminal security step from the login POST's JSON Data (pseg_client.py:1139-1169). No stage in this executable matrix can serve that body and observe it, so the kind stays in the nightly declaration and in the fast model probe instead of asserting a fixture/production mismatch as an auth invariant.

model_only.reason: The P2-03 security-step builder is HTML while production reads the terminal security step from the login POST's JSON Data (pseg_client.py:1141-1145); the kind is declared and probed at model level here and reported for P2-03/P2-09 alignment instead of being executed against a fixture production cannot observe.
